answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on misbehavior: an attacker who tries to forge a thousand fake agents must lock real capital behind each one, so the attack's cost grows linearly while its payoff does not. Reputation acts as a mirror of past conduct, and once an identity's stake falls to its nadir after repeated slashing, the network stops trusting it entirely.
